description: Roberta – AI Engineer | Flavia – Strategy & Market Intelligence Analyst. We bring together AI/ML, data analytics, strategic thinking and data-driven storytelling. For the Adapt Farm with NASA Data challenge, we aim to turn Earth observation data into practical insights for smarter and more resilient farming.
summary: AgroSense turns complex agricultural and NASA data into practical guidance for small Romanian farmers. It combines GAEZ crop suitability, modeled yields and water limitations with NASA weather and soil moisture data to help farmers compare crops and understand local conditions. It also suggests four-year crop sequences using documented agronomic principles, supporting crop diversity, soil health and the management of shared pest and disease risks.
details:
AgroSense helps small Romanian farmers compare crops and explore four-year crop sequences, initially focusing on the Bărăgan Plain.

The dashboard combines GAEZ v5 crop suitability, modeled yields and water limitations with NASA POWER historical temperature, precipitation and modeled root-zone soil saturation data. Farmers can compare eight recommended crops and understand environmental conditions through graphs and indicators.

A local language model explains options and suggests crop sequences guided by documented agronomic principles, emphasizing diversification, soil health and shared disease risks. Recommendations acknowledge missing cultivation history and other unverified constraints.

Built with HTML, JavaScript, GitHub Pages, the NASA POWER API, GAEZ data and a local LLM, Field Shift translates complex datasets into accessible guidance.

Its creativity lies in connecting crop potential, environmental history and understandable planning explanations. We considered small farmers’ limited resources, access to advice, drought exposure, usability and scientific uncertainty. Our intended impact is better-informed agricultural decisions.
